Re-checking step-by-step:

Formula: Profit = (Price - Variable Cost) * Q - Fixed Cost
where Q = units sold = min(Demand at that price, Capacity 2000)
Variable Cost = $12, Fixed = $5,000

- $19: Demand 2553 > 2000, so Q = 2000
  Margin = 19-12 = 7
  7 * 2000 = 14,000
  14,000 - 5,000 = 9,000

- $24: Demand 900, Q = 900
  Margin = 24-12 = 12
  12 * 900 = 10,800
  10,800 - 5,000 = 5,800

- $29: Demand 764, Q = 764
  Margin = 29-12 = 17
  17 * 764 = 12,988
  12,988 - 5,000 = 7,988

- $34: Demand 267, Q = 267
  Margin = 34-12 = 22
  22 * 267 = 5,874
  5,874 - 5,000 = 874

- $39: Demand 74, Q = 74
  Margin = 39-12 = 27
  27 * 74 = 1,998
  1,998 - 5,000 = -3,002

Comparison: 9,000 > 7,988 > 5,800 > 874 > -3,002
Maximum remains $19 with $9,000 profit. Earlier calculations verified correct.
